records.people: Francisco Lopes (president of the Banco Central do Brasil, 1999); Claudio Ness Mauch, Demostenes Madureira de Pinho Neto and Luiz Augusto Bragança (directors of the Banco Central do Brasil); Luiz Antonio Andrade Goncalves (director of FonteCindam)
records.summary: The president and three directors of the Banco Central do Brasil were prosecuted for peculato over the foreign-exchange operations by which the bank rescued Banco Marka and FonteCindam during the January 1999 devaluation; they were sentenced in April 2005 to 10 to 12 years, reduced on appeal to 4 to 6 years, and the 6th Federal Criminal Court of Rio de Janeiro then declared their punishability extinguished by retroactive prescription because the appeals had never become final.
records.source_title: PRR2: reus de caso Marka sao beneficiados por prescricao retroativa (Correio Braziliense, Blog do Servidor)
records.quote: O juizo declarou extinta a punibilidade dos reus pela prescricao retroativa, cerca de onze anos apos a condenacao.
records.detail: A second and distinct Brazilian episode from the 2010-2012 Copom leak investigation already on the map: different people, different years, different conduct. It rests on a newspaper legal blog rather than on the court's own published decision, so it is marked weak; the next round could seek the 6th Federal Criminal Court of Rio de Janeiro ruling itself.

records.people: Yasuyuki Yoshizawa (chief manager, Capital Markets Division, Credit and Market Management Department, Bank of Japan)
records.summary: The chief manager of the Bank of Japan's Capital Markets Division pleaded guilty at the Tokyo District Court to accepting 4.3 million yen in bribes, taken over four years from May 1993, from the Industrial Bank of Japan (about 3.16 million yen of entertainment over 58 occasions) and Sanwa Bank (about 1.15 million yen over 29 occasions), while denying that he had leaked Bank of Japan information; he had already been dismissed by the bank.
records.source_title: BOJ official admits taking bribes, denies leaking bank info (The Japan Times, 11 June 1998)
records.quote: He apologised for damaging the BOJ's standing and acknowledged that he was entertained because of his BOJ position.
records.detail: Distinct from the Fukui episode of 1999-2006 already on the map, which concerns a governor's private fund holdings rather than bribery of a division manager. Filed as charged because the source records a guilty plea at the first hearing, not a verdict.

records.category: bribery; leaking state secrets; insider trading
records.people: Former head of the monetary policy department of the People's Bank of China, identified by Caixin as Sun Guofeng
records.summary: A former head of the monetary policy department of the People's Bank of China was sentenced to 16 years and six months in prison for taking bribes, leaking state secrets and insider trading; the Supreme People's Procuratorate released only part of the official's name and his former position, and Caixin reported that the description matches Sun Guofeng, who had headed that department.
records.source_title: Ex-Central Bank Official in China Sentenced to Prison for Leaking State Secrets (Caixin Global, 28 December 2023)
records.quote: Sixteen years and six months in prison for taking bribes, leaking state secrets and insider trading.
records.detail: This passes the subject test set out in the brief: the person convicted held office AT the central bank, in its monetary policy department, and is not a commercial banker the PBOC helped to detect. Distinct from the Fan Yifei conviction already on the map, which concerns a deputy governor.

records.people: Kumar Deshraj (Assistant Treasurer, Reserve Bank of India, Chennai) and two co-accused
records.summary: An Assistant Treasurer of the Reserve Bank of India was convicted by the XI Additional Special Judge for CBI Cases in Chennai of misusing his official position under the Prevention of Corruption Act 1988, over the exchange of deliberately cut currency notes fraudulently prepared at the Reserve Bank's Chennai branch, which caused a wrongful loss of 33,81,500 rupees; he was sentenced to two years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of 15,000 rupees.
records.source_title: RBI official convicted, sentenced to 2 years RI (Press Trust of India / Business Standard, 21 November 2014)
records.quote: Two years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs 15,000 for misusing his official power.
records.detail: A second Indian episode distinct from the K. Michael arrest of December 2016 in Bangalore already on the map: different official, different city, different year, and a completed conviction rather than a charge.

records.category: procurement outside the public tender law; internal controls / spending
records.people: Turkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankasi (institution; no individuals named in the report)
records.summary: The Turkish Court of Accounts, in its 2017 regularity audit report on the Turkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankasi, found that service procurements based on the employment of personnel which had to be tendered under Public Procurement Law 4734 were instead treated as exempt and obtained without a tender, and that in the bank's outsourcing tenders contract values were not fixed at all and bid and performance guarantees were set far below the legal minimums, in two instances at 0.82 and 1.65 per cent against required floors of 3 and 6 per cent.
records.source_title: Turkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankasi 2017 Yili Sayistay Denetim Raporu (T.C. Sayistay Baskanligi, September 2018), Bulgu 2 and Bulgu 4
records.quote: Personel calismasina dayali hizmet alimlarinin, istisna kapsaminda degerlendirilerek ihale edilmeksizin temini yoluna gidildigi tespit edilmistir.
records.detail: The supreme audit institution's own report on the central bank, downloaded and read in full. Distinct in actors, years and conduct from the Emrah Sener / BKM investigation of 2023-2025 already on the map. The report names the institution and its directorates, not individuals, which is what the audit office published.

records.people: Unnamed public servants of the Banco de Mexico responsible for supervising contract 19-1147-2-Subcontrat
records.summary: Mexico's Auditoria Superior de la Federacion, auditing the Banco de Mexico's information and communications technology spending for the 2022 public accounts, issued a Promocion de Responsabilidad Administrativa Sancionatoria requiring the bank's own Directorate General of Comptrollership and Risk Management to investigate and, where warranted, open administrative proceedings against the public servants who omitted to supervise the services delivered under a specialised-services contract, in breach of the bank's own budget rules, internal payment rules and organisation manual.
records.source_title: Informe Individual, Banco de Mexico, Auditoria de Cumplimiento a Tecnologias de Informacion y Comunicaciones 2022-0-98001-20-0016-2023, Auditoria Superior de la Federacion
records.quote: Se determinaron 4 resultados... 4 Recomendaciones y 1 Promocion de Responsabilidad Administrativa Sancionatoria.
records.detail: The audit institution's own report, downloaded and read. The sanctioning action is numbered 2022-9-98001-20-0016-08-001. Distinct from the 2022 Banxico rate-decision leak already on the map, which concerns the finance minister and the president rather than contract supervision.

records.category: internal disciplinary finding against a senior official
records.people: Musa (MV) Mbhele (Managing Director of the South African Bank Note Company and employee of the South African Reserve Bank)
records.summary: The South African Reserve Bank dismissed Musa Mbhele on 21 January 2011 as Managing Director of the South African Bank Note Company and as an employee of the bank, following a formal disciplinary process; he had been suspended the previous year after weaknesses were uncovered at the South African Bank Note Company, the note-printing operation whose managing director he was.
records.source_title: Dismissal of MV (Musa) Mbhele, Managing Director of the South African Bank Note Company (South African Reserve Bank media statement, 21 January 2011, published on gov.za)
records.quote: Mbhele was suspended the previous year after weaknesses were uncovered at the SABN.
records.detail: A second South African episode distinct from the Bankorp/Absa and CIEX matter of 1985-2018 already on the map. The statement records that the Reserve Bank ran the disciplinary process and employed him; it does not state the South African Bank Note Company's ownership, so no subsidiary relationship is asserted here beyond what the statement says. The statement names a formal disciplinary process and not a specific offence.

records.central_bank: Central Bank of the Russian Federation
records.people: Andrey Tishensky and Sergey Protsko (engineers, Southern Main Directorate of the Bank of Russia)
records.summary: Two engineers of the Southern Main Directorate of the Bank of Russia were detained on suspicion of stealing banknotes from the bank's own premises, where the notes were to be destroyed with special equipment; the reported theft was about 2,000 notes of 5,000 roubles, roughly 9.77 million roubles, recorded in July 2024, and searches turned up old banknotes worth over 100 million roubles.
records.source_title: Sotrudniki TsB RF zaderzhany za khishchenie deneg, prednaznachennykh dlya unichtozheniya (Ridus, 3 August 2024)
records.quote: Dvoe sotrudnikov Tsentralnogo banka Rossiyskoy Federatsii byli zaderzhany po podozreniyu v khishchenii denezhnykh sredstv.
records.detail: This passes the subject test the brief sets for Russia: the people detained are employees of the central bank accused of taking the central bank's own money from its own premises, not commercial bankers the Bank of Russia helped to detect. Distinct from the 2005 Alexei Mishin bribery charge already on the map. It rests on a single press report of a detention; no prosecutorial or court document was located.

records.category: disclosure of bank information to outside firms
records.people: Kateryna Rozhkova (first deputy governor of the National Bank of Ukraine)
records.summary: The first deputy governor of the National Bank of Ukraine was reported to be under investigation by the Security Service of Ukraine, the State Investigation Bureau and the Prosecutor General's office over her role in sharing PrivatBank information with four specialist firms, Kroll, AlixPartners, Hogan Lovells and Asters, during the fraud investigation at that bank; the agencies were said to be compiling a criminal case, and Rozhkova said she knew of no investigation.
records.source_title: Ukrainian security investigating deputy governor - media reports (Central Banking, 19 March 2021)
records.quote: Three bodies were reportedly compiling a criminal case over her role in sharing PrivatBank information with four firms.
records.detail: Distinct in person, year and conduct from the Oleksandr Pysaruk refinancing matter of 2014-2019 already on the map. It rests on trade-press reporting of a Kyiv Post story rather than on a prosecutorial document, and the official denies knowledge of any investigation, so it is marked weak and filed only as under investigation.

records.people: Megha Mizerni (former facilities manager, Reserve Bank of Australia)
records.summary: A former facilities manager of the Reserve Bank of Australia pleaded guilty in the County Court of Victoria to obtaining property by deception, having taken about 600,000 Australian dollars from the bank by falsely issuing invoices for maintenance services over a period of roughly eighteen months; he was awaiting sentence when the report was published.
records.source_title: Ex-Employee Stole $600,000 from Reserve Bank of Australia (International Business Times Australia)
records.quote: He obtained the money by falsely issuing invoices for maintenance services for about 18 months.
records.detail: A second Australian episode distinct from the Securency and Note Printing Australia bribery case of 1999-2004 already on the map: a bank employee taking the bank's own money, not the bank's note-printing subsidiaries bribing foreign officials. The report does not give calendar years for the conduct, only its duration, and it rests on press reporting rather than on a court record, so it is marked weak.

blanks.result: searched for a second episode, found only the one already on the map
blanks.detail: The existing Canadian record is a 2004 internal-controls and spending finding at the Bank of Canada, sourced to Central Banking. No second episode was found. The Office of the Auditor General of Canada does not audit the Bank of Canada's accounts, which are audited by private firms appointed under the Bank of Canada Act, so the supreme-audit-institution vein recommended in the brief does not reach this central bank. The Bank of Canada's own annual report governance section was not opened for want of budget; that is the route a next round should take.

blanks.result: searched for a second episode, found only the one already on the map
blanks.detail: Searched in German for criminal proceedings, convictions and disciplinary proceedings against Swiss National Bank officials. Every relevant result returned was the Hildebrand affair already on the map, or its counterpart prosecution of the two Bank Sarasin employees who leaked Hildebrand's account records, which is the same episode under different actors and in any case concerns a commercial bank's employees rather than the SNB's. No second SNB episode surfaced.

The Contraloria General de la Republica search returned no audit report on the Banco de la Republica; the only Banrep page returned was its 'Organismos de control, supervision y vigilancia' page, which names the mechanism and no finding, and under the common brief's rule 2 a mechanism page is not a record. The Banco de la Republica is financially audited by its own Auditor General appointed by the President rather than by the Contraloria, so the audit-institution vein recommended in the brief does not obviously reach it. The Auditoria General del Banco de la Republica's own published reports were never opened; that is the untested route.

A real vein was located and could not be read: the Banco Central de Reserva del Peru publishes its internal audit reports at bcrp.gob.pe/docs/Transparencia/informes/informes-de-auditoria-YYYY-N.pdf, with files for at least 2016, 2020, 2023 and 2025. Three were attempted by curl and one by WebFetch; all returned an Incapsula bot-protection page of about 1,160 bytes rather than the PDF. The Contraloria General de la Republica also publishes numbered informes, several of which appeared in search behind the vlex paywall. Neither was read, so Peru has not actually been tested for a second episode; the Pizarro-era BCR bribery allegation of 1986-1991 remains its only record.

blanks.result: searched for a second episode, found only the one already on the map
blanks.detail: Searched in Russian for criminal cases, convictions and Supreme Audit Chamber findings involving the National Bank of Kazakhstan. Every result returned was the same episode already on the map: the court fine imposed on deputy chair Aliya Moldabekova over staff bonuses and the unexecuted order of the Supreme Audit Chamber, reported by tengrinews, bes.media, informburo, finratings and digitalbusiness.kz under five different headlines. No second Kazakh episode surfaced.

blanks.result: one candidate route refused on the subject test
blanks.detail: Separately from the record filed for South Africa, the VBS Mutual Bank report 'The Great Bank Heist' by Advocate Terry Motau SC was downloaded and every one of its 30-odd references to the Reserve Bank was read. The report implicates no Reserve Bank employee: the bank appears throughout as the regulator receiving false returns and as the body VBS sought to mislead. Under the brief's subject test this is the bank as detector and was refused. The Auditor-General of South Africa does not audit the South African Reserve Bank, which is shareholder-owned and audited by private firms, so that vein does not reach it either.

checked_not_in_assignment: No country outside the fifteen-code assignment was researched or filed. The Bank Sarasin employees who surfaced in the Swiss search are a Swiss matter and were refused on the subject test, not filed as another country.
leads_not_opened: TUR: the Sayistay publishes a TCMB report for every year. Four further report URLs came back in the same search and were not opened: sayistay.gov.tr/reports/download/wPoAB6Ggey-turkiye-cumhuriyet-merkez-bankasi, .../9Jo9B6Kgk7-tc-merkez-bankasi, .../14QOzjwgb3-turkiye-cumhuriyet-merkez-bankasi and kararlar.sayistay.gov.tr/reports/download/wEYD1qnoyX-turkiye-cumhuriyet-merkez-bankasi. Press coverage (medyascope, 28 September 2022) describes a later Sayistay report finding 45 million lira of payments contrary to legislation for the health expenses of some staff and their family members, and cumhuriyet describes a finding that TCMB tenders were carried out without tender. Each year is a separate third, fourth and fifth record for Turkey.

MEX: the ASF audits Banco de Mexico in most years. Only the 2022 ICT audit (2022_0016_a) was read. Simplified reports 2023_ficha_GB_a (in both IR2023a and IR2023c) and audits 2024_0038_a and 2024_0336_a were returned by the same search and not opened.

PER: the BCRP internal-audit PDF series and the Contraloria numbered informes, both described in the Peru blank. The BCRP files are behind Incapsula; a next round should try WebFetch with a different path form or the Contraloria's own site.

RUS: 'Eks-sotrudniki Banka Rossii otpravleny v tyurmu za khishchenie 585 mln rubley' (tadviser, on the DS-Bank matter) and the Regnum report 'sotrudniki TsB pomogli pokhitit polmilliarda' were deliberately NOT opened. On the brief's subject test for Russia they may well be ex-Bank-of-Russia staff acting at a commercial bank, which would not count, and deciding that needs the indictment rather than the headline.
COL: the Auditoria General del Banco de la Republica's own published reports, never opened.
CAN: the Bank of Canada annual report governance and audit-committee sections, never opened.

RUS/general: arb.ru publishes a monthly 'Prestupleniya v bankovskoy sfere' digest (e.g. arb.ru/arb/library/presuplenia-banki/prestuplenia-banki-06-2025.pdf) going back years. It is mostly commercial-bank crime, but it is a systematic, dated, searchable series and no round has grepped it for Bank of Russia staff.
